title: SQL injection in product search endpoint
summary: The product search endpoint built its database query by pasting the user's search term directly into SQL. An attacker could type database commands into the search box and read or change anything in the database — including every customer record — without logging in.
description: The `q` parameter of `/api/search` is concatenated into a SQL query string. A single quote in the input breaks the query, confirming injection. UNION-based extraction retrieved the `users` table including password hashes.
impact: Full read/write access to the primary database as an unauthenticated attacker: complete exposure of customer PII, credentials and orders, and the ability to tamper with records. This was the highest-risk issue found before launch.
stepsToReproduce: Observe a 500 error revealing a SQL syntax error
Submit q=test' UNION SELECT email,password_hash,3 FROM users--
Observe user credentials returned in the search results

evidence.title: Vulnerable query construction
UNION-based extraction
evidence.content:
GET /api/search?q=x' UNION SELECT email,password_hash,3 FROM users-- - HTTP/1.1
Host: api.arkstudios.example
Accept: application/json

evidence.title: Credentials returned in response
evidence.description: The search response contains user emails and bcrypt hashes extracted via UNION injection.

remediation.recommendation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements so user input is never interpreted as SQL. Never build queries by string concatenation. Add a least-privilege DB role for the API.
remediation.verification: Re-tested with sqlmap and manual payloads; injection no longer possible. Added a Semgrep rule to block string-concatenated queries in CI.

title: Authentication bypass on admin console
summary: The internal admin console only checked whether someone was an admin on the front-end. By requesting admin pages directly, an outside attacker could reach the admin area and act as a support operator without ever logging in.
description: The admin authorization check was enforced client-side only; the server rendered admin API routes without verifying the session role. Directly requesting `/admin/*` API routes returned privileged data.
impact: An unauthenticated external attacker could access the admin console, view all customer accounts, and perform privileged operations (password resets, account changes).
stepsToReproduce: Front-end redirects to login, but the API at /api/admin/users responds 200
Enumerate and modify user accounts via the admin API directly

evidence.title: Server route missing auth check
Unauthenticated admin access
evidence.content:
GET /api/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: admin.arkstudios.example

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
[{"id":1,"email":"...","role":"admin"}, ...]

remediation.recommendation: Enforce authentication and role authorization server-side on every admin route with a centralised middleware. Fail closed. Add MFA for admin access.
remediation.verification: All /api/admin/* routes now require a valid admin session; verified with automated tests.

title: IDOR exposes other tenants' invoices
summary: Any logged-in customer could read other customers' invoices simply by changing the invoice number in the web address. The system returned the document without checking that it belonged to the person asking.
description: The `/api/invoices/:id` endpoint fetched an invoice by ID without verifying ownership against the authenticated user. Incrementing the ID returned other users' invoices, including names, addresses and amounts.
impact: Bulk exposure of customer personal and financial data through simple ID enumeration — a full data-breach scenario with GDPR implications.
stepsToReproduce: Log in as a normal user
Observe other users' invoice data returned

evidence.title: No ownership check

remediation.recommendation: Scope every object lookup to the authenticated owner, e.g. add `AND user_id = $2`. Add automated authorization tests for horizontal access. Consider non-sequential IDs as defence in depth.

title: Stored XSS in support ticket messages
summary: A customer can put hidden code inside a support message. When a support agent opens the ticket in the admin console, that code runs in the agent's browser — letting an attacker take over the agent's session.
description: Ticket message bodies are rendered as raw HTML in the admin console. A payload such as `` executes in the agent's authenticated context, enabling session theft and actions as the agent.
impact: Escalation from a normal customer to an internal admin session: an attacker who files a malicious ticket can hijack a support agent and pivot to admin capabilities.
stepsToReproduce: Open a support ticket as a customer
Set the message body to
Wait for an agent to view the ticket

evidence.title: Unsanitised render
evidence.content:
<div className="ticket-body"
  // BUG: renders attacker-controlled HTML
  dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: message.body }} />

remediation.recommendation: Render ticket content as text, or sanitise with a strict allow-list (DOMPurify). Add a Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline scripts. Set HttpOnly on session cookies.

title: Session cookie missing HttpOnly and Secure flags
summary: The login session cookie was not marked HttpOnly or Secure, so it could be read by page scripts and sent over unencrypted connections — making session theft much easier if any other flaw (like XSS) exists.
description: Session cookies lacked HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite attributes, increasing the impact of XSS and network interception.
impact: Amplifies other issues: a session cookie readable by JavaScript turns any XSS into full account takeover.

evidence.title: Insecure cookie options

remediation.recommendation: Set httpOnly:true, secure:true and sameSite:'lax' on session cookies; shorten lifetime and rotate on privilege change.

title: Missing rate limiting enables OTP brute force
summary: The one-time-code check for login has no limit on attempts, so an attacker can rapidly try every 6-digit code until one works — defeating two-factor authentication.
description: `/api/auth/verify-otp` accepts unlimited attempts with no lockout, backoff or CAPTCHA. A 6-digit OTP (1,000,000 combinations) is brute-forceable within the code's validity window at achievable request rates.
impact: Two-factor authentication can be bypassed by brute force, undermining a key account-protection control.
stepsToReproduce: Trigger an OTP for a target account
No throttling; a valid code is accepted

remediation.recommendation: Enforce per-account and per-IP rate limits with exponential backoff, lock after N failures, expire OTPs quickly, and add anomaly detection.
